context: Make the OpenCode Go provider survive refresh, restore, uninstall and drift: catalog as committed data, a reconciling refresh script, the Claude launcher with its full install-plan wiring, the domain terms, and the operator guide.
root_causes: The declared catalog was a Python constant, so a model added upstream was listed by live discovery but not routable, and refreshing meant editing code.
A new backend claiming an id OpenCode publishes does not trip G1's conflict guard, because config rows are claimed first and the catalog-owning seed defers, so the id moves silently.
LAUNCHER_CATALOGS feeds the client_sync install plan, whose group and surface contracts are pinned in code AND mirrored in a manifest, so adding a launcher row alone fails closed.
The catalog spans 202752 to 1050000 tokens but a launcher is rendered once, so no single static context window is per-model correct.
evidence: Adding the launcher row alone failed 26 tests with 'manifest Claude launchers drift from launcher catalog'; the full wiring required EXPECTED_GROUPS, EXPECTED_SURFACES and the manifest to agree.
Adding opencode to REVERSO_ROUTED_CODEX_PROFILE_PREFIXES cascaded to 83 failures because codex-sync then requires live OpenCode model discovery per sync and fails closed without it.
A monkeypatched kimi claim over glm-5 does not raise ModelIndexConflictError; the resulting index maps glm-5 to kimi, and it is the exposure --check that fails.
The committed catalog matched the live catalog at 29 ids when reconciled by the refresh script.
solutions: Move the catalog to docs/reference/opencode-go-catalog.json, read by both the listing fallback and the routing declaration, failing closed on a corrupt or empty artifact.
Add a refresh script whose --check diffs committed against live and prints added and removed ids.
Land the Claude launcher with the provider group, the shared-reverso-launcher dependency, the surface entry and both halves of the two double-entry contracts.
Use the catalog minimum as the launcher context window, since compacting early is recoverable and overflowing the real context is not.
Assert both gates explicitly: G1 for two index-claiming backends, the exposure check for an id leaving the bare set.
Defer the Codex profile and route to its own slice rather than half-landing the Codex client-sync surface.
acceptance_criteria: A model added to the catalog artifact becomes routable with no code change.
The artifact is the single source for both the listing fallback and the routing declaration.
A corrupt or empty artifact fails closed rather than declaring an empty catalog.
The refresh --check fails closed on drift and names the added and removed ids.
A genuine two-backend collision fails with a message naming both backends and saying what to do.
A silent transfer of a bare id away from OpenCode is caught by the exposure check.
The claude-opencode launcher installs with its group, dependency and surface contracts consistent in code and manifest.
The launcher pins no single model and sets both window variables.
CONTEXT.md gains the catalog-owning backend, bare exposure and incumbency terms.
Operator documentation covers key provisioning, quota versus opt-in versus outage failures, and per-request provider attribution.
legacy_risk_reason: changes the client_sync install plan contracts and the launcher catalog shared by every provider; a regression breaks install or uninstall for all of them, and can leave user-owned files modified
